The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the **last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria)**.  
That ancestor was a small, insect‑eating mammal that lived roughly 100 million years ago, long before the split that produced the separate lineages of carnivores (lion) and odd‑toed ungulates (zebra). There isn’t a named species for this ancestor; it’s simply the ancestral node that gave rise to the entire clade of placental mammals.
